resulted in a change in the level of function
decline in intellectual function that is
severe enough to compromise social/work function
: stroke, family hx, DM, smoking, HTN, obesity, TBI hx, hearing loss, vitamin D deficiency, chronic sleep deprivation, more common in females (may be due to longer life expectancy)
: physical activity, education, ongoing intellectual stimulation, social engagement – all promote cognitive reserve, an improved capacity to compensate for insidious neurodegeneration
*MC insidious onset & gradual progression of sxs
•exclude occult cerebrovascular disease, tumor, other structural abnormality
B12, TSH/FT4, RPR, HIV, CBC, electrolytes, glucose, lipids
: target cognitive symptoms, do not prevent disease progression
: NMDA antagonist approved for moderate-severe Alzheimer
short-term memory impairment early & most prominent feature
•variable deficits of executive function, visuospatial function, & language
accumulation of cognitive deficits in associated w/ repeated strokes; sxs depend on stroke location
occur in the brainstem, midbrain, olfactory bulb, & neocortex +/- Alzheimer pathology
w/ anxiety, visual hallucinations, & fluctuating delirium
: neuropathology is variable & defined by the
•Tau protein, TAR DNA-binding protein 43 (TDP-43), or fused-in-sarcoma (FUS) protein account for most cases
deficits in empathy, social comportment, insight, abstract thought, & executive function
& ↓ interest in sex or sweet/fatty foods
deficits in word-finding, single-word comprehension, object & category knowledge, & facial recognition
; behaviors may be similar to behavioral variant FTD
speech is effortful w/ dysarthria, phonemic errors, sound distortions, & poor grammar
